transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in because I just keep getting these nagging thoughts that I forgot something important. It's usually stuff like, um, worrying I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or that I didn't set up my classroom materials safely for the kids at school. And... even when I know I probably handled it fine, the doubt just keeps popping back into my head.

When you get these nagging thoughts about forgetting something or handling something unsafely, do you feel driven to do something to check or fix it—like going back to verify that the medicine was set up correctly, or rechecking your classroom materials?

Yeah, I do. Before I leave the house, or before I lock up my classroom for the day, I’ll usually go back over the same things a few times. I end up checking her pill organizer, or making sure the stove is off, or looking through my lesson plans again. 

Sometimes it's not even physically checking, I just... silently replay what I did in my head to make sure I didn't mess up. I basically have to keep doing it until I feel calm enough to actually move on and leave. It does end up making me run late sometimes, but I just feel like I need to be sure.

Besides worries about forgetting things or handling things unsafely, do you ever get other kinds of intrusive thoughts—like concerns about things being in the wrong order, or needing things to be symmetrical or 'just right,' or other nagging thoughts that don't fit into the safety or harm category?

No, not really. It's pretty much just the stuff I mentioned. I don't really care if things are perfectly lined up or anything like that. It's really just the worrying that I forgot something important or left something unsafe.

When you have these thoughts about forgetting things or leaving things unsafe, do you recognize that these worries might be excessive or irrational, or do they feel completely reasonable and necessary to you?

I'm... not really sure. I mean, I know it's probably a bit much to check the same thing three or four times, but when I'm actually in the moment, it just feels completely necessary to me. Like, if I don't do it, I won't be able to stop worrying. So I guess I don't really know if I'd call it irrational, but I do know it's probably more than what most people do.

When you're checking these things multiple times, do you recognize in that moment that the checking probably won't actually help you feel more certain, or does it feel like the checking is genuinely necessary and will help?

Well, like I said before, when I'm actually doing it, it feels like I have to. Like before I leave the house or lock up the classroom, I'll go back over the same things a few times—checking her pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans, or just replaying it all in my head. In the moment, it feels like the only way I'll get calm enough to actually leave, even though I know it makes me run late sometimes. It just feels like I need to do it to be sure.

Looking back on times when you've had these worries about forgetting things or leaving things unsafe—after you've checked multiple times and left the house or classroom—do you realize afterward that your worry was probably unfounded, or do you still believe something bad might have actually happened?

I guess once I'm actually driving to school or heading home, I usually feel okay. I don't really sit and think about whether the worry was completely unfounded... I just know I checked everything, so it should be fine. 

I mean, since nothing bad has ever actually happened, I guess looking back I know it was probably just me worrying too much. But I don't really analyze it like that after the fact. I mostly just feel relieved that I got the checking done and I can finally move on with my day.

When you're in the moment checking these things, if someone told you that you've already checked enough times and that nothing bad is actually going to happen, would you be able to accept that and stop checking, or would you feel like you absolutely have to keep going?

I don't think I could just stop. If my husband or someone told me I'd checked enough, I'd probably just feel... annoyed, honestly. I'd still feel that physical need to do it myself until it felt right to me. Even if they said it was fine, their word wouldn't fix that nagging feeling in my head. I'd still have to finish my routine, or I wouldn't be able to let it go.
